title: Shadow Tenancy: burst testing and cost-safety for GPU pools
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This document describes the "shadow tenancy" pattern for safely validating multi-tenant burst behavior on GPU pools. Shadow tenancy allows tenant workloads to be executed in a mirrored (non-billing, non-production-affecting) mode against live-serving infrastructure so we can validate batching, KV-cache warming, preemption reactions, and cost signals before permitting live-burst traffic. The objective is to reduce production surprises from burst events while collecting realistic telemetry to tune autoscalers, billing signals, and rollback guards.

Motivation
----------
- Tenants requesting burst capacity today frequently uncover latency regressions, cache-miss storms, or billing anomalies after go-live.
- Current preflight/eval sandboxes produce synthetic load that doesn't capture live routing, prefix cache distributions, and multi-tenant interference.
- We need a low-risk, repeatable opt-in path to test tenant burst profiles against the allocator, cache, and egress rate limiters without affecting live billing or SLOs.

High-level design
-----------------
1. Shadow placement: the allocator (service: allocator-v2) creates a mirrored allocation for a tenant request with identical resource sizing and network path, but with the following differences:
   - traffic mirror flag set so requests are forked (1:1) and routed to the shadow session;
   - shadow sessions use a restricted policy: no external side-effectful calls allowed (e.g., webhooks disabled);
   - shadow KV cache writes are local-only and marked non-authoritative.
2. Billing isolation: shadow sessions are routed to a dedicated shadow accounting namespace (metering key: shadow-test) that is excluded from billing exports.
3. Telemetry and labels: every shadow request includes tenant_id, shadow_run_id, and experiment_tag. Metrics flow to a separate Prometheus scrape job and a shadow metrics index in Cortex/Grafana for comparison.
4. Safe-fallback: if shadow session causes node-level instability (OOM, kernel-panics, GPU ECC errors), the node is automatically cordoned and the owner-team is paged. No production session is evicted by a shadow session.

Components and responsibilities
--------------------------------
- allocator-v2: implements shadow session allocation and metadata propagation. (Owner: infra / serving-runtime)
- burst-orchestrator: controls when a tenant can opt into shadow tenancy for burst requests and records opt-in policy. (Owner: infra / capacity)
- billing-exporter: filters shadow-test namespace entries from bill pipeline. (Owner: finance-integrations)
- telemetry pipeline: dedicated shadow metrics index + dashboards. (Owner: observability)
- ci-cd: terraform module and CD pipeline to toggle tenant shadow flags. (Owner: ci-cd / infra)

SLOs and thresholds for shadow runs
----------------------------------
- Shadow-run health SLO: 99.0% of shadow requests must complete (non-HTTP-side-effect) in <= 95th percentile of baseline for that tenant.
- Safety thresholds that trigger immediate abort of the experiment:
  - Node GPU memory pressure > 90% sustained for 1 minute;
  - GPU ECC error rate spike > 5x baseline in 5m window;
  - p95 latency for shadow requests > 3x tenant baseline for 5m.

Terraform / IaC module spec (conceptual)
---------------------------------------
We will provide a terraform module that creates the shadow namespace, IAM bindings, and toggles mirror rules in the allocator. Example usage (YAML-like pseudo):

module "tenant_shadow" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/redwood/iac.git//modules/tenant-shadow"
  tenant_id = "tenant-1234"
  enable_shadow = true
  mirror_ratio = 1.0                  # 1:1 fork for full fidelity; allowed range 0.0 - 1.0
  max_concurrent_shadow_sessions = 10 # throttle to limit resource occupancy
  safety_policy = "cordon-on-gpu-ecc,abort-on-latency"
}

Configuration table (module variables)
-------------------------------------
Name | Type | Default | Notes
-----|------|---------|------
tenant_id | string | n/a | tenant namespace id to shadow
enable_shadow | bool | false | must be explicit true to opt-in
mirror_ratio | float | 0.0 | fraction of requests mirrored (0.0-1.0)
max_concurrent_shadow_sessions | int | 1 | soft cap to limit warm-pool consumption
safety_policy | string | "default" | policy id that maps to safety checks in the orchestrator

CI/CD integration and gating
----------------------------
- Pipeline: terraform module changes land in git in the iac/modules/tenant-shadow folder.
- Unit tests: go tests + terratest that validate module plan does not modify billing exporter or production namespaces.
- Integration: a protected CD pipeline (deploy-shadow) runs in a non-blocking mode for 24h; only after shadow-run artifact passes stability checks in the shadow metrics dashboard is the tenant allowed to promote mirror_ratio to >0.5 for larger scale tests.
- Approvals: changes that set enable_shadow=true for production tenants require a two-person review from capacity and security teams.

Runbook: enabling a tenant in shadow tenancy
-------------------------------------------
1. Preflight (owner: solutions-eng)
   - Confirm tenant test plan and measurement prompts.
   - Ensure tenant has a dedicated shadow_run_id and an experiment_tag.
   - Notify oncall and observability owners with scheduled window.
2. Deploy IaC (owner: infra-ci-cd)
   - Create branch and submit terraform change to set enable_shadow=true, mirror_ratio=0.05, max_concurrent_shadow_sessions=2.
   - Run terratest; ensure no plan diffs touch billing-exporter.
   - Merge to protected branch and trigger deploy-shadow pipeline.
3. Early validation (owner: tenant-ops, 30–60 minutes)
   - Observe shadow metrics dashboard: request completion rates, per-request latency, cache-hit ratio.
   - Compare shadow metrics vs baseline using the provided diff-panel.
4. Escalation and abort criteria (owner: oncall)
   - If any safety thresholds are tripped, toggle enable_shadow=false via emergency CLI (redwood infra cli shadow disable --tenant tenant-1234) and runnode cordon.
5. Promotion steps (owner: capacity)
   - If metrics are stable for 24h at mirror_ratio=0.05, increment mirror_ratio to 0.25 and repeat validation.
   - Final full-fidelity validation (mirror_ratio >= 0.9) requires 72h of stable shadow runs and finance sign-off to proceed with billing-path changes.

Monitoring and dashboards
-------------------------
- Shadow overview dashboard (Grafana folder: Shadow Tenancy) showing:
  - Shadow vs baseline p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap
  - KV-cache warmup curves for mirrored sessions
  - Node-level GPU memory and ECC error overlays
  - Shadow session occupancy vs warm-pool capacity
- Alerting rules (Cortex alerts):
  - shadow_request_failure_rate > 1% for 10m -> P3 alert to tenant-ops
  - node_gpu_memory_pressure > 90% -> immediate P1 page to infra-oncall
  - shadow_latency_anomaly_detector (ML based) -> routed to capacity owners

Telemetry and offline analysis
----------------------------
- All shadow traces are tagged with experiment_tag and stored in the shadow traces index.
- Weekly run comparisons are scheduled as part of the burst-validation board (notebooks: workloads/shadow-comparisons).
- We keep shadow telemetry for 30 days by default; retention can be increased for long-running experiments with approval.

Security considerations
-----------------------
- Shadow sessions are blocked from performing external side-effects: denylist enforced in the egress-proxy (webhook hosts, external DBs).
- Secrets: shadow sessions cannot access production KMS keys; a shadow-only key must be provisioned if any crypto is required.
- RBAC: enabling shadow tenancy for a tenant requires explicit IAM role redwood.shadow.operator.

Costs and accounting
--------------------
- Shadow runs consume compute and may therefore reduce available warm pool capacity; we must cap concurrent shadow sessions to avoid impacting live tenants.
- Billing exporter will always exclude the shadow-test namespace; finance will still be able to see shadow consumption in an internal cost center for experiment accounting.

Open questions and next work items
----------------------------------
- How to automate safety_policy selection per-tenant based on historical volatility.
- Should we provide synthetic request fuzzers to amplify edge-case cache misses inside shadow runs?
- Explore ability to retroactively replay production traces into shadow sessions without live forking.

-------------
